method.selection: All @[goal] in tracked Lean; all theorem/lemma/abbrev/def in Solidity/Theorems.lean; top 30 public theorems by distinct direct importers of their defining module, ties path then line. This is module exposure, not declaration usage. Includes examples explicitly.
method.generated: Roots, Corpus, AxiomPins, and first-1600-character generation markers separated; unmarked is not a handwriting guarantee. Chain/agreement generators may lack markers; no scale verdict uses this approximation.
method.parsing: Source-level, not elaborated. Premises column is explicit binders; arrows remain in conclusion. Context preserves open/variable commands, including commands from earlier ended sections; consult source for exact scope. No proof rechecked.
method.ratios: Reference theorem statement logical-obligation ratios only; no unjustified LOC/check-time comparison of compiler vs calculus. Source citations are cited, not measured. Compiler header nonblank physical line ratios are descriptive typography only; outliers justified by abbreviation/scope, never treated as effort or strength. Other rows have no like-for-like compiler-pass counterpart.

timings.use: Existing sample only; no per-selected-theorem timing inferred

references.statement:
Theorem transf_c_program_correct:
  forall p tp,
  transf_c_program p = OK tp ->
  backward_simulation (Csem.semantics p) (Asm.semantics tp).
references.status: measured pinned source excerpt; source not compiled
references.comparison: Successful actual translation implies backward simulation of C to assembly; source undefined behaviour constrains guarantees. Intrinsic-model soundness is a different boundary.

references.statement:
Theorem compile_semantics:
   precondition interp s env cfg ec prog
 ⇒
   ¬semantics_determ s env prog Fail ⇒
   semantics_determ s env prog
      (semantics ec s.ffi s.ptr_eq_oracle (SND (compile cfg prog)))
references.status: measured pinned source excerpt; source not compiled
references.comparison: A verified pass: non-Fail source semantics and explicit precondition imply equality of source and compiled flat semantics; not a Solidity or full-backend theorem.

conclusion: Headline calculus theorems match their stated intrinsic-model scope. Compiler statements retain payment/refusal and abstraction gaps against behavioural refinement. Source examples are useful fixed-case checks, not general semantic preservation. No evidence here justifies judging overall project size redundant.
